title: Tech & architecture slides for the Aktia deck
subtitle: Two slides for deck-writer: architecture replaces the 'Technical solution architecture' slide; gates and risks goes after the compliance slide
footer: Recordly | Aktia | Ticket-to-merge-request analytics developer agent

slides.title: The agent drafts, a person merges: one loop inside Aktia's tenant, with no path around review
bullets: **No bypass, enforced technically:** the agent's identity has no approve, merge or admin right. Branch protection and CODEOWNERS are owned by Aktia admins. Schema-dependency paths also need the data owner. The reviewer is never the ticket requester.

**Model hosting is Aktia's choice, with the residual exposure named:** open-weight model in your tenant (no external provider in the call path); EU-headquartered provider (external call, DORA register entry); hyperscaler or Snowflake-hosted model in an EU region (EU residency, but a foreign-HQ provider). One swappable interface, exit tested.
**Stack assumed, confirmed in week 1:** on Snowflake + dbt we deploy our agent team; on another stack the agent is a new build, and scope is re-agreed at the gate.

slides.title: Three technical gates before the agent touches real work, and the failure risks we design for
bullets: **Week 1, integrations:** stack, ticket system, Git host and CI confirmed; bypass test passes (push or merge as the agent identity fails).
**Week 3, Definition gate:** hosting options run on 20 of your tickets and reported with their exposure; Aktia compliance picks one or stops. Baseline set: rework rate, review minutes, lead time.
**Week 9, pilot gate:** approved-without-rework rate, review minutes per PR and cost per ticket vs. baseline. Targets set at week 3; a miss means stop or adjust.
table: Plausible but wrong PR; reviewer fatigue and rubber-stamping
Reasoning summary in every PR; review minutes and approval trend tracked; sampled second review
Prompt injection or vague text in a ticket
Ticket treated as untrusted input; agent can only open a PR a person rejects; unclear tickets go back
Flaky tests give a false green
Tests re-run; a pass that a reviewer rejects is counted and reviewed
Provider or model version changes behaviour
Pinned versions; test set replayed before any switch; worse result blocks release
No model option is good enough or accepted
Scope narrows to simple ticket types, or Aktia stops at the gate
Retry cap; it stops and writes what it tried
slides.note: Unknowns: ticket volume and quality, ticket-system API or webhook, run cost per ticket (measured in Definition, then a monthly cap and alert). Aktia compliance signs the control matrix; we do not certify.
